chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh ibn Nusayr, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), whenever he wanted some necessities for himself or something of a personal nature, would write to my father, meaning Ali: 'Purchase for me this and that, and acquire for me such and such, and let Hisham ibn al-Hakam undertake that for you.' But if it had to do with his more general responsibilities, he would just write to him: 'Purchase for me this and that,' and not mention Hisham unless it was personal. It is mentioned that his care and attention towards him was so great that he sent him fifteen thousand dirhams, saying to him, 'Work with it and keep all the profits, but return the principal to us.' Hisham, may Allah have mercy on him, did so, and prayers upon Abu al-Hasan.

key_terms.هِشَامُ بْنُ الْحَكَمِ: Hisham ibn al-Hakam, a prominent companion and agent of the Imams

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Kadhim manage his personal finances and compensate his agent Hisham ibn al-Hakam?
ai.summary: This narrative from Rijal al-Kashshi highlights the financial management practices of Imam al-Kadhim (peace be upon him), specifically his personal trust in Hisham ibn al-Hakam for private transactions. The Imam provided Hisham with a significant capital sum, instructing him to keep the profits as compensation while returning the principal, a practice that underscores the Imam's endorsement of Hisham's commercial acumen and integrity. This arrangement reflects the broader Shia scholarly understanding of the Imams' engagement with worldly affairs to sustain their communities and validate their trusted deputies.
